prize_parts.citation: for developing methods to estimate demand and competition in differentiated-product markets, which made empirical industrial organisation a quantitative tool for analysing market power, mergers and policy

statement.case_for: My configuration has changed. In round 1 I put B014 first and B005 first among my alternatives, and I called the two close. After the exchange I now put B005 first. I apply one test to all four leading candidates: did the work change what the profession can credibly know, and has that been validated by use and scrutiny over time? B005 meets it most directly. Berry, Levinsohn and Pakes (1995) solved a specific problem, estimating demand for differentiated products with endogenous prices and unobserved quality, while keeping a structural link to theory. Pakes' dynamic-industry strand extends it. The methods are about three decades old and are routine in merger review, antitrust and regulation, and in trade, health and environmental work. Colleagues describe a long record of critique and refinement, which I take from their statements and have not verified. On methods versus discovery, I accept the argument of Teorell, Enflo and Friberg: a measurement advance that makes market power, substitution and welfare effects estimable from data is itself a discovery. The attribution core is also contested less than on any other candidate. All five B005 supporters now name Levinsohn as third, and Friberg changed his opening choice of Bresnahan. I keep the citation on demand and competition in differentiated-product markets, so that it names one achievement. A citation that widens to the earlier new-empirical-IO tradition would have to change the credit set too, and I would not make that substitution inside this citation. I do not treat the five supporters as evidence of merit. What moved me is that the reservations I conceded for B014 (identification, overlap with 2024) are ones its own supporters share. The reservation I hold on B005, that it is a toolkit, is one I now think the common test answers.
statement.case_against: B005 is a methods prize without one headline substantive finding. The committee may reasonably weigh that against candidates that explain policy choice (B014) or conceptual mechanisms (B027). The three-name cap leaves out Bresnahan and Reiss, who founded the new empirical IO tradition, and Benkard and Levin on the dynamic side, so the exclusions are real. BLP-type estimates are sensitive to functional form, instruments and implementation, so the citation should not suggest settled magnitudes. Moving away from B014 also gives up its substantive reach. Political economics turned loosely connected questions into a field with formal models and tests, and I still think that field is underrated on the criteria of maturity and attribution. I treat the identification and overlap concerns as a reason to rank it second, not as a reason to dismiss it.

responses.point: Fredriksson ranks B014 first. He says the citation must separate policy outcomes under political rules from the long-run institutions agenda, that Besley's state-capacity strand is the part most exposed to the 2024 overlap, and that he would fall back on a Persson-Tabellini core and name B005 as his main alternative.
responses.response: We largely agree on B014's substance. I made the same distinction between policy choice under given rules and the historical origins of institutions, and I still think it is real. But the exchange shows that the distinction has to be argued. Your own note that Besley's strand sits closest to the 2024 agenda means the cleanest B014 award would be two people, which gives up the coherent three-person credit set that was part of my first-round case. A Persson-Tabellini prize would also have to word the citation carefully to avoid overclaiming causal findings from cross-country evidence. Taken together, those costs move me to B005. I keep B014 as my first alternative. If you and others find the overlap and identification points answerable, I would regard a Persson-Tabellini citation as the defensible form of that case.

responses.point: Teorell ranks B005 first and B014 second. He argues that the 2024 recognition rested on a design that supports a causal reading, whereas the constitutional and electoral-rule evidence relies more on cross-country comparison. He also says the committee should expect to be asked why institutions are being recognised again so soon.
responses.response: This is the argument that did most to move me. In round 1 I rested distinctness on the topic: policy under given rules rather than long-run prosperity. You add a point about evidential standard, which I had conceded only as a weakness. A second institutions-related prize would invite scrutiny of its identification, and the B014 evidence is weaker on that dimension than the 2024 evidence was, on your account. I cannot verify the committee's 2024 reasoning from the files I have, so I take it as your statement. I also take your point that treating methods as lower-status on principle would be a bias, and I want to avoid that. On my round-1 reference to a possible Persson link in your opening: I cannot re-read that file in this stage, so I do not rely on it. Your round-1 statement that the profile shows no such tie is what I take as your disclosure.

responses.point: Friberg ranks B005 first and revised his third name from Bresnahan to Levinsohn. He argues that breadth of use beyond industrial organisation is the common criterion, and he asked for a more detailed discussion of which B014 results are well identified and whether the Persson-Tabellini and Besley strands are one achievement.
responses.response: I think your request is fair, and I cannot meet it from the evidence I have. Neither my round-1 statement nor the other openings separate the well-identified B014 results from the weakly identified ones. I should not ask the committee to credit a field on an assurance I cannot back with detail. I agree that breadth of validated use is the right test for a candidate like B005, with one caution I hold from my own work. Breadth of use does not by itself settle which discovery a prize should reward, and I would not apply it mechanically against conceptual contributions such as B027. I also note that you and I have co-authored, so my agreement with you should not be read as independent confirmation. My move rests on the identification and overlap arguments above, not on your preference.

responses.point: Krusell ranks B027 first. He says B014's identification problem is unresolved and that the committee should state what B014 adds beyond institutions and prosperity. He also concedes that B005 has a documented record of use, whereas the Kiyotaki-Moore mechanism is more indirectly validated.
responses.response: Your request to state what B014 adds is one I tried to answer in round 1, and I now think the answer is not decisive enough for a first choice. I still rate B027 as a clean two-person contribution, and I keep it as an alternative. The main thing separating us is the weight on conceptual originality versus validated use. You were open that indirect validation is the weak point of your own case, and I think that candour is correct. Under the single test I applied above, direct validation counts for more, which puts B005 ahead of B027 for me. I would not claim that settles the ranking if the committee weighs originality more heavily. On the 2022 overlap, your distinction between bank runs and intermediation and collateral-constrained borrowers seems reasonable to me, but I have not verified it independently.

responses.point: Boppart ranks B027 first. He was moved by the B005 argument, but still says the B005 credit set is diffuse and that implementation sensitivity is a concern. He also warns that agreement among Hassler, Krusell and himself is not independent confirmation.
responses.response: I accept your warning, and I have recorded the co-authorship in my conflict note. I read the B005 diffuseness concern as largely resolved once the citation is limited to demand and competition in differentiated-product markets. The three-person core is then not contested among the supporters, and the open question is which broader strand a different citation would add. On implementation sensitivity we do not fully agree. I read it as a limitation on how estimates are used and as a sign of long scrutiny. I do not read it as an objection to the originality of the method. It does mean the citation should avoid language suggesting settled magnitudes.

uncertainties: Whether the committee will judge a methods and measurement contribution to be at least as weighty as a substantive discovery or a conceptual mechanism. The committee has not agreed on one test across B005, B014, B027 and B030.

Whether the third name should be Levinsohn or Bresnahan, which depends on whether the citation rests on the BLP estimator or on the broader new-empirical-IO tradition. I have not verified the details of either claim independently.

How much of B014's evidence is well identified, and whether the 2024 overlap should be treated as a bar or only as a weight. I moved on a judgement here that others reasonably make differently, and I am not sure it is right.

Claims about replication records, the 2022 and 2024 prizes, and the history of the field come from colleagues' statements and my own recollection, and I have not verified them. This is the limit of my evidence.
statement.conflict_note: Updated from round 1. My preferred part is now B005, and my profile lists no co-authorship or institutional tie to Pakes, Berry or Levinsohn. My round-1 field proximity to B014 (dynamic political economy) no longer applies to my first choice, although B014 remains my first alternative, and I list no tie to Persson, Tabellini or Besley. I disclose that I have co-authored with committee colleagues Friberg (menu costs, IJIO), Boppart and Krusell, and that I am an IIES colleague of Krusell and Boppart. Friberg, whose arguments I answer, works in industrial organisation, and I was influenced by his position, so my movement toward B005 should not be read as independent of his. My profile records no tie to any other shortlisted credited name. I note and do not adjudicate the discrepancy about Teorell, which I cannot resolve from the files available to me in this stage.
